clue.text: Style said to be warped by traditionalists for a start, anti-bourgeois

parts.note: a DA (duck's arse) is a slicked-back 1950s hairstyle

indicators.note: warped means bent out of shape, so the letters of said are twisted into a new order
for a start points to the opening letter of traditionalists

explanation.surface: Someone's style is reportedly corrupted by old-fashioned types, yet it is rebellious against middle-class values.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style said' looks like a homophone, but 'said' is anagram fodder: 'to be warped' turns SAID into DAIS. DA is the hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an art movement scornful of conventional, middle-class taste, so a follower of it is against the bourgeoisie.

clue.text: Idiotic supporting cruel feeding swindle in fast food chain

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the word for idiotic sits below the rest
feeding means the word for cruel goes into the word for swindle

parts.note: a do is a con or swindle, as in 'it was a real do'
unkind means cruel
nuts means crazy or idiotic

explanation.surface: A daft scam involving nasty practices at a burger outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunkin' Donuts is an American chain selling coffee and doughnuts, a fast food brand.

clue.text: See 1
Enthusiastic about country's rise and fall?

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone keen on the rise and fall of their homeland's fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise and fall' suggests a nation's history, but it means the pitch of the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise and fall of pitch in speech is what linguists call its tonal melody.

clue.text: After a rise, police on good rates

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise sends the word for police upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
pi is short for pious, i.e. good

explanation.surface: Following an increase, police are charging good rates.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, a musical pace or speed.

clue.text: Soft item with no end to flatten, not this then?

indicators.note: with no end tells us to drop the final letter of the word for flatten

parts.note: to fell is to knock flat, as with a tree or opponent
if not this one, then the other one: that

explanation.surface: A puzzled shopper wonders whether some soft thing, endlessly squashable, is the one to reject.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat made of felt is soft and crushable, unlike a hard hat or bowler.

clue.text: Moving freely, ankle screws removed?

definitions.meaning: unrestricted, free to go where one likes
with the fixings out, the lower limb would be unattached

explanation.definitionFit: Being free of ties means able to roam freely; literally, a foot that is no longer fixed in place.

clue.text: Sumptuous boozer

explanation.definitionFit: Lush means rich or luxurious, and as a noun it is slang for an alcoholic.

clue.text: A bounder stood up amid laughter — why no sex tonight?

indicators.note: amid places these letters in the middle of the laughing sound

parts.note: he-he is the sound of laughter

indicators.note: in a down clue, stood up turns the word for bounder upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a cad is a bounder, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rogue is stood up on a date and laughed at, leaving no romance tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood up' looks like a missed date, but in a down clue it turns the bounder upside down; 'amid' sets that inside the laughter. The definition is the classic excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not tonight, I've got a headache' is the clichéd excuse for declining intimacy.

clue.text: Bird circling ridge to find tropical plant

indicators.note: circling means the seabird surrounds the word for ridge

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
a reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the sea surface

explanation.surface: A seabird circles a coral ridge in search of tropical vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree ferns are large palm-like ferns with trunks, growing in tropical and subtropical regions.

clue.text: Person in book group

indicators.note: in places the word for person inside the abbreviation for the book

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
one means a person, as in 'one should know better'

explanation.surface: Someone belongs to a reading club.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, an ensemble name like quartet or quintet.

clue.text: Desolate scene where love in poems can degenerate

indicators.note: in tells us the zero letter sits within the rearranged words
to degenerate is to decline into a worse state, so the letters of poems can collapse into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A bleak landscape where romantic verse loses its quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degenerate' rearranges POEMSCAN, and 'in' slots O (love) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunar landscape is barren and cratered, so the word is used for any bleak, empty terrain.

clue.text: Machinations of Belgian in Poirot ultimately impossible to grasp

indicators.note: machinations are scheming plots, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement
ultimately picks the final letter of Poirot

explanation.surface: The schemes of Agatha Christie's Belgian detective are beyond comprehension.
explanation.walkthrough: Poirot really is Belgian, which makes 'Belgian in Poirot' read as description rather than fodder. 'Machinations of' rearranges BELGIANIN plus T, the last letter that 'ultimately' takes from Poirot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intangible cannot be touched or grasped, physically or mentally.

clue.text: Knee higher — this lower?

definitions.meaning: the part of the leg that has the knee above it
one that lows, i.e. a young cow that moos

explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy back of the lower leg sits below the knee, and a young bovine lows, making it a 'lower'.

clue.text: A marked village showed wart, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of showed wart are jumbled

explanation.surface: A village displayed a blemish, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marked' means bearing a mark: this Devon village's name includes an exclamation mark, Westward Ho!
explanation.definitionFit: Westward Ho! is a seaside village in Devon, the only English place name officially carrying an exclamation mark.

clue.text: See 25
Plain wet to practise excessively

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view
the wet means rainy weather, so rain

explanation.surface: An ordinary soggy person is trying too hard at training.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to exercise or rehearse beyond what is beneficial, too much practice.

clue.text: For example, tit measurement spawning novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of spawning take a new form

explanation.surface: A new way to measure a small bird, inspired by its breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A tit is a small bird, and the span from wingtip to wingtip is one measurement of it.

clue.text: Bread — Croatian money?

parts.note: Split is a city on the Croatian coast
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Bread as slang for cash: what do they call it in Croatia?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like the money slang, but it is a loaf; a split tin is a British loaf baked in a tin with a split along the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A split tin is a white loaf with a lengthwise crack across its crust, a type of bread.

clue.text: See 28
Hint — problem with cue?

definitions.meaning: a warning or piece of inside information
a snooker cue whose leather end has come away

explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a discreet warning; literally, a cue with its end detached.

clue.text: One tucks into revolting gruel, less appealing

indicators.note: tucks into means the numeral is pushed inside the jumbled letters
revolting means rebelling, so the letters of gruel rise up and rearrange

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone digs into disgusting porridge, finding it even less pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like a description of the gruel, but it is the signal to rearrange it into UGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglier is the comparative of ugly, meaning less pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Step by entrance, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the word for entrance is only heard, spelt differently

parts.note: a gate is an entrance to a field or garden

explanation.surface: Someone takes a step beside a doorway, or so they tell us.
explanation.definitionFit: Gait is a manner of walking, one's characteristic step or stride.

clue.text: Daydreaming male catching end of member on a zip

indicators.note: catching means the male deer holds the letter within it

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, or a man without a partner

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of member

parts.note: zip and zing both mean energy or liveliness

explanation.surface: A man gets his member caught in his zip while his mind wanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts R, the letter 'end of' takes from member, inside STAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stargazing is to be lost in idle thought, gazing skyward instead of attending.

clue.text: Qualification for Bellerophon, say?

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a statement or document that modifies it
Bellerophon in Greek myth mounted the winged horse Pegasus

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added condition on a contract, and also someone on horseback like Bellerophon on Pegasus.

clue.text: Precious little deeper than bottom of pit

indicators.note: in a down clue, deeper than means the word for little sits below the letter
in a down clue, the bottom of pit is its final letter

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small treasure lies just beneath the floor of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means affectedly dainty or cute, which is one sense of precious.

clue.text: Deduce how to make a square?

definitions.meaning: to reason out a conclusion from evidence
two plus two gives four, a square number, so adding two and two is one way to make a square

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to draw the obvious conclusion from available facts; literally, adding two and two gives four, which is two squared.

clue.text: Indian garment pinned back by pandit — oh dear

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
pinned says the letters are held fast inside the words that follow, running from one word into the next

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Indian loincloth is fastened behind by a learned man, who sighs in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'pinned' in the definition, but it is the hidden-word indicator: 'pinned ... by' holds ITOHD inside 'pandit — oh dear', and 'back' turns it round. The definition is just 'Indian garment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth wrapped around the waist and legs, worn by men in India.

clue.text: Material in bread, sharp

parts.note: naan or nan is an Indian flatbread
keen means sharp, as a blade or wit

explanation.surface: A fabric somehow tucked into a pungent loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing, so it is a fabric.

clue.text: Part of house in need of refurbishment? It could be better

definitions.text: Part of house in need of refurbishment?
definitions.meaning: a chamber that is ripe for doing up, read literally
said of performance that leaves scope for getting better

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scope for getting better; literally, a chamber awaiting renovation.
